sampling_model.design: Two independent fixed-size arms sample from \(K\) equal-probability covariate cells. The primary parameter is a pair of deterministic sign arrays in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\). The lower experiment is indexed by \(q\in\mathcal R_K^{\circ}(r)\) and mixes only over the legal shell \(|\rho_K-q|\le s_K\).
sampling_model.units: Within each arm, observations are independent. Conditional on a sampled cell, the outcome is Bernoulli with the cell probability \(p_{dj}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Arm membership is fixed by the two-sample design; treatment and control samples are independent and no unit appears in both arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell has sampling probability \(1/K\) in each arm, while cross-arm overlap is governed by \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The amplitudes \(a\) and \(b\) are known. The sign arrays are unrestricted apart from membership in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\); the procedure estimates their empirical cross-arm correlation only through collision marks. Continuous transfer uses \(U_{di}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and is compared with the discrete design only after the measurable pushforward \(\mathsf Q_K\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives general sharp conditional optimal-transport bounds, and Theorems 2--6 develop continuity and statistical guarantees for their estimation.

Proposition 3.2 supplies the key estimation bound, Proposition 3.3 supplies the quadratic-objective stability inequality, and Theorem 3.2 establishes asymptotic normality for quadratic COT under smooth positive densities.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid dual lower confidence bounds even under an arbitrarily inaccurate outcome model, while later results give sharpness under nuisance-rate conditions.

The public manuscript characterizes sharp optimal-transport identified intervals and gives root-\(n\) sample-analogue inference for potential-outcome functionals in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model.
Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 transfer a sharp multinomial-uniformity testing lower bound using supported Poisson mixtures and a conditional central limit theorem.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize minimax expected-measure confidence sets through Bayes--minimax duality and test inversion.
Propositions 1 and 2 give uniformly valid confidence intervals for interval-identified parameters with explicit treatment of the identified-set-length nuisance.
Theorem 3 proves local asymptotic minimax efficiency of Bayes estimators in nonregular parameter-dependent-support experiments.
Theorem 1 bounds total-variation error for Poisson approximation of locally dependent rare-event counts and processes.
The published minimax analysis identifies collision-dominated behavior for testing uniformity of sparse Poisson data under missing-ball alternatives.
The coincidence statistic attains the sparse-alphabet sample-complexity threshold for uniformity testing through explicit collision moment bounds.
Poissonized and density-estimation experiments are asymptotically equivalent above a Besov regularity frontier and can fail to be equivalent below it.
Finite-sample optimal confidence intervals balance worst-case smoothness bias against variance for average treatment effects under unconfoundedness.

body.tldr: For binary outcomes on a growing uniform covariate partition, the setup identity gives the sharp absolute-cost COT lower endpoint \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\), where \(\rho_K\) is the realized correlation of two deterministic sign arrays. When \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\) stays finite and triple collisions vanish, nearly all information about \(L_K\) is carried by a Poisson number of cross-arm collisions with weak binary marks. The proposal establishes an exactly indexed interior-lattice supported-mixture comparison with parameter-free forward and reverse kernels, a uniform deterministic-array collision approximation, exact minimax absolute-risk and honest-length transfer, and computable rational interval-action certificates whose tail, off-grid coverage, and rounding errors are explicit. When \(\lambda_K\) diverges sparsely, the same collision estimator becomes uniformly studentized Gaussian; the open kernel is the matching local minimax theorem on deterministic Hamming shells. Continuous transfer is limited to the coarsening pushforward of an explicit uniform-covariate interpolation image, because arbitrary coarsening changes the COT endpoint without a separate bias bound.

project_justification.gap: Published COT theory supplies sharp identification, consistency, rates, model-agnostic conservative inference, and smooth quadratic-cost inference through Proposition~3.2's key estimation bound, Proposition~3.3's quadratic-objective stability inequality, and Theorem~3.2's central limit theorem, but it does not characterize the non-Gaussian information experiment created by sparse cross-arm replication on a growing partition. Large-alphabet collision theory and confidence-set duality supply techniques, not the two-arm marked endpoint or legal deterministic-array transfer.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a single information frontier indexed by expected cross-arm collisions: exact finite-information decisions when \(\lambda_K\) is bounded and Gaussian local efficiency when \(\lambda_K\) diverges, always centered at the actual sharp finite-array endpoint.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a marked-Poisson reduction with parameter-free forward and reverse randomization on an explicit interior correlation lattice under shell-conditioned legal product mixtures, derives uniform collision-statistic approximation for every deterministic array, and certifies honest finite-information intervals by exactly checked rational lower-dual and upper-primal witnesses with explicit Poisson-tail and continuum-coverage corrections. It resolves the remaining LAN-to-shell lower bound before transferring only after a measurable coarsening pushforward from an explicit uniform-covariate interpolation image.

body.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS, Theorems 1--6) establish general sharp COT bounds, continuity, and statistical guarantees; Theorem~1 supplies the identification formula of which the affine binary endpoint is a setup specialization, while their remaining results inform the estimation setting without yielding a rare-collision experiment. Their smooth-density follow-up (2026) uses Proposition~3.2 for the key estimation bound, Proposition~3.3 for the quadratic-objective stability inequality, and Theorem~3.2 for asymptotic normality; the binary absolute-cost model instead requires marked-collision likelihood theory. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.5) deliver model-agnostic dual inference and emphasize binning loss, but do not optimize honest expected length or identify the collision frontier. Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) is an unpublished manuscript deriving sharp OT intervals and root-\(n\) sample-analogue inference for potential-outcome functionals in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model; it informs the OT-inference comparison but does not study sparse covariate collisions or deterministic-array transfer. Paninski (2008) and Kipnis (2026) show that collisions govern sparse large-alphabet testing; Kipnis's Theorems~2.1 and~2.3 in arXiv:2607.05223 provide the closest conditional-central-limit and supported-mixture architecture, although their object is one-sample uniformity testing. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, Theorem 1) supply the forward dependency-neighborhood approximation. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1) supply test inversion and Bayes--minimax duality for expected measure, while Stoye (2009, Propositions 1--2) shows why boundary nuisance sequences require uniform coverage analysis; neither source supplies the Poisson-tail truncation, likelihood modulus, endpoint expansion, full-interval repair, or exact rational primal--dual verification required for a continuum-parameter certificate here. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem 3) provide the limits-of-experiments efficiency template; exact deterministic Hamming shells and the ordered truncation limits are new obligations here. Low and Zhou (2007) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2021) inform the restricted pushforward transfer and bias-aware scope, without supporting a claim over a full smoothness ball.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The former two-fixed-array lower witness is invalid because armwise marginal imbalance reveals the endpoint without cross-arm collisions. Every lower bound in this core therefore uses mixtures supported on legal arrays and targets the realized \(L_K\). Floating-point linear-program output may only suggest candidate witnesses: a certificate exists only after every likelihood and tail coefficient is outward-rounded and the resulting rational primal and dual inequalities are verified exactly. Endpoint decisions may be clipped to \(\mathcal D\) without increasing absolute or squared loss, but projection of the statistic \(\widehat L_K\) onto the narrower range \(\mathcal A\) is excluded from the local Gaussian theorem because it changes boundary risk.
body.honest_scope: The finite-\(\lambda\) experiment comparison, decision transfer, convergence of the rational interval-certificate bracket, sparse studentized central limit theorem, deterministic-shell efficiency identity, and interpolation-image pushforward transfer are all to be proved. The affine binary COT identity and the exact zero- and one-mark formulas are setup and sanity propositions, not novelty claims. At \(\lambda=0\), the result reduces to the no-information bounded-parameter risks \(R(0)=br\) and \(C_\alpha(0)=2br(1-\alpha)\). The interval certificate covers computable \(\lambda\), including rational inputs, through certified shrinking rational enclosures; an uncertified floating-point value is outside the claim. No raw total-variation comparison is made between mutually singular continuous covariates and discrete labels. No claim is made for unknown amplitudes, nonuniform cell probabilities, nonnegligible triple collisions, dense cellwise estimation, or a full continuous smoothness class. Coarsening changes the estimand unless a separate bias theorem is added.
